home.introbox: Fake news from 1945. The Nazi propaganda film »Theresienstadt« uses images and music to conceal the true conditions in the concentration camp. This learning application helps to recognise propaganda and manipulation, provides insight into the involuntary protagonists and shows the filming locations.
home.everydaylifebody: The film suggests a carefree daily life characterised by leisure, sport and play.
home.workbody: Manufactories, workshops and farming suggest economic self-sufficiency.
home.culturebody: Publicly performed concerts, operas and lectures suggest artistic freedom at a high level.
home.news-description: Latest news and updates about the »Theresienstadt Explained« project.
home.origin-description:
Filming in the Theresienstadt ghetto 1942–1945,
by Eva Strusková, Jana Šplíchalová, Tomáš Fedorovič, Václav Kofroň
home.persons-description: Short profiles of the people who appeared as protagonists in the propaganda film – mostly under coercion and without knowledge of how the footage would be used.
home.scenes-description: An annotated overview of all 38 scenes of the film with information on location, people and historical context.
home.places-description: An interactive map of the filming locations and historical settings in the Theresienstadt/Terezín ghetto.
home.fake-video-description: How modern AI manipulates video footage – historical film propaganda compared with today's deepfake methods.
home.propaganda-headline: Manipulation and propaganda in the film
home.propaganda-description: The film did not document the reality of the concentration camp, but staged a fictitious world – using deliberate techniques to deceive the global public.
home.guided-video-description: A moderated screening with commentary on propaganda techniques and historical background.
home.film-analysis-description: A collaborative analysis tool with which learners can jointly identify and discuss propaganda techniques in the film.
home.references-description: Recommended documentaries, books and essays on Theresienstadt and Nazi film propaganda.
